newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says 1996 truck sales down 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says 1996 truck sales down 17 pct.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Friday that its 1996 truck sales fell 17 percent to 63,682 vehicles.
The decline in Volvo's truck sales stemmed from a fall in North and South America, where total markets were considerably smaller last year compared with 1995, the company said in a statement.
In Europe, Volvo's truck unit consolidated its position as the second largest manufacturer of heavy trucks, the company said.
In total, Volvo delivered 63,682 trucks in 1996, of which about 5,000 were in the medium-duty segment. In 1995, the company's truck sales totalled 76,489.
In North America, Volvo sold 16,855 trucks last year, down 38 percent from 27,092 vehicles in 1995, the company said.
In South America, Volvo's sales fell 36 percent to 4,982 trucks in 1996 from 7,798 units the previous year.
Deliveries in Europe amounted to 35,030 trucks last year, little changed from 35,190 vehicles in 1995.
In Europe, Volvo increased its market share for heavy trucks to 16.8 percent in November, 1996, from 16.2 percent for 1995, the company said.
